## Opponent Reads

**Player 2**: **LAG/maniac.** 3-bets extremely wide (trash hands). Calls down light, barrels with air. Folds to 3-bets from tight players (P1, P5, P6). **On dry boards: c-bets flop but checks/folds turn when called — profitable float spot.** Self-destructive over time — confirmed losing chips across all 3 sessions (busted S1, below-start S2, -$195 S3). **Exploit**: 3-bet them for value. Value bet thin in single-raised pots. Do NOT bluff them. Float dry-board c-bets.

**Player 3**: **Selectively aggressive, skilled but variance-prone.** Opens and 4-bets WIDER than premium: 4-bets suited aces as semi-bluffs. Actively 3-bets from SB against late-position steals. **Postflop trapping tendency**: Checks draws on flop, leads turn when completing. River checks can be traps. On dry boards, folds to aggression without connections. **REVISED**: NOT "consistently near starting stack" — had a major losing session (-$245 in S3). Their wide 4-bet bluffing catches up to them. **Exploit**: C-bet dry boards. On wet boards, their checks ≠ weakness. When they lead turn after checking flop = likely completed draw. Don't value-bet thin on river. Can call wider vs their 4-bets. Tighten steal range when P3 is in blinds.

**Player 4**: **Wide VPIP (~47%), passive preflop, dangerous accumulator.** Consistently finishes above starting stack across all 3 sessions (+$130 S3). Limps weak, raises better hands. 3-bets 99+, shoves AA over 4-bets. **EXTREMELY sticky caller** — confirmed calling river with 9-high and bottom pair. Check-raises with strong hands only. **Exploit**: Isolate limps with position. 4-bet lighter vs their 99-QQ. Value bet EXTREMELY wide — they call with air. NEVER bluff them. Respect check-raises. #1 value target at table.

**Player 5**: **Ultra-nit preflop (~6% VPIP) BUT more effective than label suggests.** Surged to +$265 in S3 despite tiny VPIP — extracts maximum when they play. Any preflop raise/3-bet = extreme premium. **Postflop**: Donk-bets made hands (folds to raises/turn barrels). With strong draws: donk-bets AND shoves. **Exploit**: Fold to preflop aggression unless premium. Two-barrel bluffs effective vs made-hand range. Be cautious raising donk-bets on draw-heavy boards. Don't underestimate — when they play a pot, they win big.

**Player 6**: **Tight raiser (~9%) with wide limping range (K8o-level).** Chip leader S3 (+$305), accumulates effectively. 3-bets = QQ+/AK. Cold 4-bets = AA/KK. Flat-calls opens from blinds with TT-JJ/AQ, folds these to 3-bets. **Sticky with premiums postflop.** Can take initiative on turn when opponents show weakness. **Exploit**: Fold to their 3-bets/4-bets. Isolate limps freely. Do NOT bluff postflop. Squeeze over their blind flats.

**Player 7**: **Tight preflop, bleeder.** Defends blinds with pairs and speculative hands. Peels flop/turn but folds river without strong hands. Folds to flop check-raises. Will stab rivers with air when sensing weakness. **Consistently loses across all sessions** (-$205 S3). **Exploit**: Three-barrel bluffs effective. River bets from them after passive action = potential bluff. Isolate their BB.

## My Table Image & Strategic Assessment

**3-session pattern (CRITICAL)**: 60 hands played, won ~18 contested pots, ALL through fold equity. ZERO showdowns across entire sample. My entire profit engine is fold-equity dependent.

**The problem**: Winning $15/steal but losing $25-85 when facing resistance (AKo -$85 in S3). One big loss erases 5-6 successful steals. Net result: gradual chip decline (-$55 S3).

**Image risk**: After 60 hands without showing a hand, sharper opponents (P3, P4) may begin exploiting by attacking my folds. My TAG image is built on betting patterns alone with no confirmed evidence of hand strength.

## Core Strategy Adjustments for Next Session

1. **MUST get to showdown with a winner.** Actively seek spots to stack off with premiums rather than always folding to resistance. A shown winner reinforces image for dozens of future hands.
2. **Stop bleeding with marginal hands.** K7s, A8o in raised pots = dominated. Either 3-bet as a bluff or fold. Don't flat and face further aggression.
3. **Continue pressure game** but recognize its ceiling: thin margins from steals require near-zero big-pot losses to be profitable.
4. **Threat hierarchy**: P3 (skilled, wide 4-bets) > P4 (dangerous station) > P6 (sticky nit) > P5 (extractive nit). P2 and P7 most exploitable.
5. **Board texture**: Dry = bluff freely. Wet = only with equity or heads-up. Multiway wet = give up without a hand.
6. **Postflop nit distinction**: P5 CAN be bluffed (two-barrel). P6 CANNOT be bluffed.
7. **Table over-folds to tight aggression** — exploit with steals/3-bets but don't erode image.
8. **When P3 is in blinds**: Tighten steals or prepare 4-bet/call strategy for their 3-bets.

Shows tendency to check-fold turn after c-betting flop — indicates bluff-heavy c-bet tendency or weakness when facing resistance. - Against stations (Player 4), thin value betting works well — they call down too light.  
- Against tight folders (Player 2, Player 3), 3-bet bluffs are highly profitable.

**Opponent Profiles & Tendencies:**
- **Player 1 (LAG / Spewy):** Highly aggressive and prone to overplaying. Opens extremely wide preflop (including offsuit K-high trash). Capable of massive multi-street bluffs with pure air, and will frequently take delayed stabs when flops check through. 
- **Player 2 (Extreme LAG / Calling Station):** Plays a very wide range (will open and call 3-bets OOP with medium suited gappers/connectors) and 3-bets light from the blinds. Post-flop, they are an absolute station—floats very light (e.g., check-calling with bottom pair) and capable of calling river shoves on scary boards with marginal hands. They barrel marginal hands on scary boards. *Exception:* In single-raised pots defending the Big Blind, they play straightforwardly and will fold to small c-bets on dry boards.
- **Player 4 (Aggressive / Extreme Station):** High VPIP/PFR but also capable of limping absolute garbage (e.g., 97o) from middle position. Crucially, their 3-bet range includes many non-premiums, and they will fold to 4-bets, but they DO balance this by 5-bet jamming their actual premiums (AA). Post-flop, they are capable of mind-boggling spew and station behavior—they will call turn bets with weak gutshots and even call river bets with absolute air (9-high). *Note:* They do have a folding button on the river if the board becomes extremely scary (e.g., 4-to-a-straight, 3-to-a-flush) and they face heavy aggression.
- **Player 5 (Passive / Recreational):** Classic limp/caller preflop, but will open-raise strong hands. Post-flop, they make probing donk-bets. *Crucial Note:* While some donk-bets are weak, they will play strong draws (like nut flush draws) extremely aggressively, donk-betting flops and open-shoving turns. Their preflop 3-bets represent an incredibly strong premium range.
- **Player 6 (Mixed TAG/Passive):** Previously thought to be tight, but they are capable of open-limping weak offsuit broadways (e.g., K8o) from early position. Their 3-bets still represent a very strong, value-heavy range (premiums and AK). Post-flop, they can be somewhat sticky, floating flop donk-bets with just AK-high, and will value bet two-pair hands on the river even on flush-completing boards. They are also capable of taking the betting lead on the turn and river after check-calling the flop.
- **Player 7 (Loose / Station):** Capable of overcalling post-flop with marginal made hands (e.g., underpairs with no draw) on scary or coordinated boards, even facing multiple opponents. Will also make small stabs/bluffs on the river with pure air when the action checks down.

**Strategic Adjustments & Exploits:**
- **Vs. Player 1:** Widen your bluff-catching range. Do not over-fold to their post-flop aggression; be prepared to call down with marginal made hands, especially when they stab at pots that check through.
- **Vs. Player 2:** NEVER bluff post-flop. Value bet relentlessly and go for maximum value (including overbets/shoves) even on scary runouts. Do not rely on flop check-raises as bluffs, as they float very wide. In blind-vs-blind or late-position steals, small c-bets on dry boards are highly profitable.
- **Vs. Player 4:** Generally NEVER bluff them post-flop. They will call down with literal air. Value bet them relentlessly and thinly. Preflop, target them with isolation raises when they limp, and exploit their wide 3-betting range by 4-betting them (for value and as a bluff), but ALWAYS fold your 4-bet bluffs to a 5-bet jam, as they are not bluffing when all the chips go in preflop.
- **Vs. Player 5:** Be cautious when raising their flop donk-bets on draw-heavy boards, as they are capable of shoving over the top with strong draws. Over-fold to their preflop 3-bets.
- **Vs. Player 6:** Give immense respect to their preflop aggression (3-bets), but realize their limping range is much wider and weaker than expected. You can isolate their limps wider. 
- **Vs. Player 7:** Value bet thinly and avoid bluffing, as they will call down with weak, marginal holdings. Can bluff-catch their small river stabs if the hand checks down.

**Self-Image & Future Adjustments:**
- **Table Image:** Previously established a very tight image, but recently showed down a light 4-bet/call preflop with A8s in a massive pot. Opponents may now perceive me as looser or more aggressive preflop.
- **Next Session Adjustment:** Re-tighten preflop calling standards in bloated pots. Strictly avoid bluffing the massive stations (Players 2, 4, and 7) post-flop. Play a pure, relentless value game against Player 4 in particular, and do not level yourself into calling 5-bet jams with marginal blockers.

STRATEGIC ADJUSTMENTS:

- **Player 7** remains a **confirmed nit** (VPIP ~6%, PFR 0%): plays only **premium hands preflop** and **folds to multi-street aggression postflop**. **Bluff effectively on wet/dynamic boards**, but **avoid bluffing on dry/static boards**. **Leads small rivers with air or weak hands**—**call more liberally with second pair+ on dry boards**. **Blind defense is passive and premium-only**—**continuation bet and barrel turns aggressively when they call preflop**. **New insight**: Player 7 **will raise preflop only with premiums**, and **folds to flop raises without top pair or better**—**flop check-raises or large bets are highly effective**.

- **Table dynamics**: **River bluffing is virtually nonexistent outside Player 2**. Most players **fold by the river without strong hands**, making **thin value betting consistently profitable**. **Multi-street aggression is common**, but **only Player 2 bluffs across streets**. **Floating and delayed aggression works well vs. Player 2 and Player 4**, but **Player 4’s cold-call/3-bet lines are strong**.

- **My table image is tight and respected**, generating **high fold equity**, especially vs. TAGs and nits. To maintain balance and maximize EV:
